findings:
FINDINGS OUTSIDE THE CLAIMS: none substantiated.

I examined two candidates and rejected both as findings against this unit; each becomes a referral instead, for the reason the brief's "Already established" clause fixes.

OBSERVATION (not a finding, no fix owed by this unit) — the report's § Deviations item 1 is superseded, not false. Report `:201-212` states the probe residue is present and names the removal as `rm -rf /home/user/fleet/ndjson/tmp/probe` for the Orchestrator. The tree shows the removal happened: `/home/user/fleet/ndjson/tmp/probe/buffer.test.ts` does not exist and no path under `tmp/` exists. The report was true when written and the deviation it raised is now closed by the action it requested. At retention, record in `.orkestrel/campaign/conform/` that the removal landed and who took it, so the retained report does not tell the next reader the residue is still on disk. This blocks nothing.

REFERRALS — to the Orchestrator, since I hold every lane this round. Neither carries a verdict from me.

R1 — the transcriptions do not gate the `clear()` comment claim in three fences, and one test is named for a behaviour its case does not exercise. `.claude/rules/tests.md:70-72` requires the transcription to "assert the values its comments claim". The Surface fence's `guides/ndjson.md:39` comment claims "drop any buffered partial - ready for a fresh stream", the Methods fence's `guides/ndjson.md:93` claims the same, and the README fence's `README.md:39` claims "drop buffered partial line - reuse for a fresh stream". None of those claims is gated. Traced against `src/core/NDJSONParser.ts:31-44`: in the Surface case (`tests/guides.test.ts:199-207`) the call at `:203` ends its chunk with `\n`, so `#buffer` is already empty when `parser.clear()` runs at `:204` and the assertion at `:206` passes identically with `clear` replaced by an empty body. The Methods case (`:235-243`) has the same shape at `:240`. The README case (`:251-258`) does not transcribe the fence's `clear()` line at all. The test at `:199` is also named "returns the Surface fence values and clears back to a fresh stream" while proving nothing about clearing. Why it matters: the row that created this file exists to close exactly this class of gap, and a `clear` that stopped clearing would leave three published fences false with the `guides` gate green. Mitigating: `clear` is genuinely gated elsewhere, at `tests/src/core/NDJSONParser.test.ts:210-240`, so the gate chain as a whole would still redden. Why this is a referral and not a finding: the assertion sequence is the refuter's own operative repair, prescribed verbatim in `conform-ndjson-brief.md:49` clause (a) including the words "to prove the fresh stream", and the test name follows the fleet precedent at `/home/user/fleet/sse/tests/guides.test.ts:190`, which carries the identical vacuity. The unit implemented what it was ruled to implement. What right looks like, if the Orchestrator rules the ruling wrong: in `tests/guides.test.ts:199-207` and `:235-243`, insert one buffering call before the `parser.clear()` line — `expect(parser.parse('{"partial"')).toEqual([])` — so that omitting `clear` leaves `{"partial"` prepended to the next chunk, makes that line malformed, and reddens the trailing assertion; leave the presence guards untouched, since the fence text does not change. Note that the same defect sits at `/home/user/fleet/sse/tests/guides.test.ts:190-199`, so this is a fleet pattern and belongs in a fleet row rather than in an ndjson-only fix.

R2 — the guide documents a return-type spelling the package's own source does not use and its own lint forbids. `guides/ndjson.md:46` (Types table Shape column), `:51` (Types fence signature), and `:84` (Methods table Returns column) all spell the return type `readonly Record<string, unknown>[]`, while `src/core/types.ts:15` and `src/core/NDJSONParser.ts:31` declare `ReadonlyArray<Record<string, unknown>>`. The unit proved the guide's spelling is unlintable in this repository: `typescript(array-type)` refused it at `tests/guides.test.ts:177:62` (report `:225-232`), which is why the transcription had to depart from the prescribed text. A consumer copying the published fence into an Orkestrel-style project gets a lint error from a fence this package ships. `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Parity requires TypeScript and Markdown to agree. This is pre-existing — both spellings predate the diff — and the unit escalated it correctly under its deviation contract as § Deviations item 3, explicitly naming it the Orchestrator's call and refusing to work around it. It therefore does not impugn this tip. What right looks like: in a successor unit, rewrite `guides/ndjson.md:46`, `:51`, and `:84` to `ReadonlyArray<Record<string, unknown>>`; update the presence-guard string at `tests/guides.test.ts:221` to the new fence text in the same edit; and delete the substitution note from the `feed` doc block at `tests/guides.test.ts:176-181`, which then describes a difference that no longer exists.
